analysis.evidence: אֵלֶּה stands as the subject of the verbless clause אֵלֶּה תוֹלְדוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ, “These are the generations of the heavens and the earth.” Its plural form agrees with תוֹלְדוֹת.
analysis.morphology: Common plural demonstrative pronoun without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: אֵלֶּה introduces the account with “these are.” The construct form תוֹלְדוֹת takes הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ (“the heavens and the earth”) as its complement. בְּהִבָּרְאָם (“when they were created”) places the formula in the context of creation.
analysis.gloss: account of the heavens and the earth
analysis.sense: generations, the account of what came from someone

analysis.evidence: הַשָּׁמַיִם is paired with וְהָאָרֶץ. The plural suffix in בְּהִבָּרְאָם (“when they were created”) refers to both, presenting heaven and earth together as the whole of creation.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ + common noun, masculine plural absolute.

analysis.evidence: הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ pairs the heavens and the earth. The plural suffix in בְּהִבָּרְאָם, “when they were created,” refers to both, identifying the earth as the terrestrial part of creation.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ plus definite article הָ plus common noun, singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: The plural suffix refers to הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ, the heavens and the earth. The Niphal presents them as receiving the action, and the parallel phrase בְּיוֹם עֲשׂוֹת describes the same event as the time when YHWH God made earth and heavens.
analysis.morphology: Temporal preposition בְּ + Niphal infinitive construct of בָּרָא + third-person masculine plural suffix ם, the subject of the infinitive.

analysis.evidence: בְּיוֹם is followed by the infinitive construct עֲשׂוֹת. Together they introduce a temporal clause, “when YHWH God made earth and heavens.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed preposition בְּ.
analysis.sense: the time when; on the day that

analysis.evidence: בְּיוֹם עֲשׂוֹת means “when … made.” יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject, and אֶרֶץ וְשָׁמָיִם (“earth and heavens”) are what he made. The preceding בְּהִבָּרְאָם (“when they were created”) confirms the creation sense.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: In בְּיוֹם עֲשׂוֹת יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים אֶרֶץ וְשָׁמָיִם, יַהְוֶה names the one who made earth and heavens. אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to the name, giving the phrase “Yahweh God.”
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, uninflected, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In עֲשׂוֹת יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים אֶרֶץ וְשָׁמָיִם, אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה. Together they identify the one who made earth and heaven.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with singular reference. No prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶרֶץ וְשָׁמָיִם names what YHWH God made. It reverses the opening pair הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ, confirming that אֶרֶץ denotes the earth paired with the heavens.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, common gender, singular absolute, without article, prefix, or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶרֶץ וְשָׁמָיִם ‘earth and heaven’ reverses the opening pair הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ ‘the heavens and the earth’. Together the two nouns express the whole of what God made.
